name: Vaash Heist

dialogue.message: Another deal gone horribly wrong with the Vaash. This time, the loss was devastating.
dialogue.response: Why are you still doing business with them? They've betrayed you before.

dialogue.message: After our arrangement to acquire the Cron-Stabilizers, we believed some trust had been re-established. We took a risk.
dialogue.response: What happened?

dialogue.message: They traded a number of highly sought-after relics for our "kevrex", a dense substance used for intergalactic travel. The Vaash have been trying to develop that technology themselves for eras.
dialogue.response: You mentioned you do not trade such technology.

dialogue.message: Normally, we do not. But we had been searching for these relics for a very long time, and the Vaash provided seemed irrefutable proof of provenance. The relics turned out to be fakes... though very convincing ones.
dialogue.response: And now they possess the kevrex...

dialogue.message: For now. It is a "fuel" of sorts — useless to them without the rest of the technology. We have a plan to take it back, but we cannot do it ourselves.
dialogue.response: Explain.

dialogue.message: Kevrex has one unique characteristic: stored improperly, it leaks a strong "trail" of energy — one that can be traveled to.
dialogue.response: But the Vaash are in an entirely different galaxy.

dialogue.message: We have the means of opening a tiny waypoint to the kevrex from here. A being your size — maybe two — could fit through it.
dialogue.response: A heist? But... why us?

dialogue.message: Our laws are complex. Certain provisions prohibit us from stealing from the platforms they operate.
dialogue.response: Even if some of the equipment was yours?

dialogue.message: Yes... even so. Technically, a deal was a deal. But nothing prevents us from helping you take it yourself.
dialogue.response: It sounds dangerous. I assume these Vaash platforms are well defended.

dialogue.message: Standard patrol drones... but lethal if you are caught. Go through the waypoint, take the kevrex and whatever else you can find, and return before the waypoint closes.
dialogue.response: What is our take?

dialogue.message: We keep the kevrex. Whatever else you find is yours — and the Vaash keep quite a number of things in their hold.
dialogue.response: Alright. We're in.

dialogue.message: I suspected you might be.
dialogue.response: Anything else we should know?

dialogue.message: The Vaash are methodical — Their drones would operate in a predictable pattern. Use that to your advantage.

rules:
Reach the relic crate without being seen, within the move budget. You move one step (or wait), then every drone moves one step along its posted route. Step into a scan cone, share a tile with a drone, or run out of moves — the run ends.

Decoy: freezes the nearest drone for 2 turns and turns its cone toward the decoy. Throwing one uses your turn.

Four drones, one decoy, and a single spare move on the clock.

Service hatches teleport you to their twin. The exit side is only safe when the nearby patrol faces away.

Faint cones show where each drone will scan next turn. Crates block movement and sight.

name: Cursed Crew

dialogue.message: Your bridge has become... quieter. Have you noticed?
dialogue.response: What have you done to my crew?

dialogue.message: Nothing that you haven't already subjected them to. I simply offered them different choices. In a way, I am freeing them of your continued enslavement.
dialogue.response: You are no savior.

dialogue.message: On the contrary. Every one of them has served your ambition for years, doomed billions on your orders, and been given nothing but rank and rations. I offer them purpose.
dialogue.response: Purpose? You offer them nothing but fear.

dialogue.message: And you do not? You spread fear freely across thousands of worlds. I am collecting what is owed.
dialogue.response: Owed to whom? This... ritual of yours?

dialogue.message: Yes. I see far, far ahead of their lifetimes... and their involvement is key. My suggestions are only temporary.
dialogue.response: I don't believe you...

dialogue.message: Your concern for them is misplaced. You will have their minds back... but for now, they are mine.
dialogue.response: What is your aim with this... ritual of yours? Why do you keep involving us?

dialogue.message: As I've said plainly before, the souls of this timeline are integral in a great casting. But... more minds are needed. More blood must be spilled.
dialogue.response: We want no part of it.

dialogue.message: Oh, its far too late to abstain. You have already joined the spell.
dialogue.response: Leave our ship. Now.

dialogue.message: Such persistence... such impatience. I am going nowhere until we are finished.
dialogue.response: We'll see about that.

rules:
3 of your 10 crew are cursed. You win when all cursed crew are quarantined.

Each turn, Ask a crew member or Quarantine one. An asked crew member states their role and one fact about the current situation. They can be asked again, possibly for new information, after 2 turns have passed.

Trusted roles:
Interrogator — names one crew member and whether they are trusted or cursed.
Medic — names two crew, at least one of whom is cursed.
Sentry — names several crew and exactly how many of them are cursed.
Cursed roles:
Whisperer — claims a trusted role and gives false information.
Corruptor — claims a trusted role and gives false information. One trusted crew member also gives false information until the Corruptor is quarantined.
Mimic — claims a trusted role and gives false information. The Mimic does not register as cursed to the Sentry.
A wrong quarantine wastes the turn. That crew member stops answering questions and can no longer be cursed. You lose after 3 wrong quarantines.

Every 4 turns, the curse converts one trusted crew member.

A correctly quarantined crew member reveals their true role and confesses that one other crew member is trusted.

Hover a crew member or a statement to see it drawn on the board as arrows from the speaker to the crew they name: red arrows mean the speaker calls them cursed, blue arrows mean trusted, dotted means one or some of the many.

You lose if the cursed count reaches 7, if 14 turns pass, or if the timer expires.
